activity.notes: Dionysius I seized effective control of Syracuse in 405 BCE after securing election as general plenipotentiary and establishing a personal tyranny. He remained ruler until his death in 367 BCE. ATLAS uses the historically appropriate role Tyrant rather than King, and binds the Activity to Syracuse rather than projecting his wider Sicilian sphere of influence as a separate empire.
